title: Lecture 1 - Complexity Basics MCQs
description: Midterm MCQs on concepts, mathematical reasoning and proof steps. No code tracing or code-analysis questions.
subject: Algorithm Analysis

questions.question: Which property is required of an algorithm?
options: It is written in a particular programming language.
It terminates after finitely many unambiguous steps.
questions.correctAnswer: It terminates after finitely many unambiguous steps.
questions.explanation: Termination and clear steps are part of the definition; recursion and constant time are not.

questions.question: Why compare algorithms by basic-operation growth instead of only stopwatch time?
options: Growth analysis reduces dependence on the particular machine.
Every machine executes every operation in one second.
questions.correctAnswer: Growth analysis reduces dependence on the particular machine.
questions.explanation: Measured seconds depend on hardware, compiler and implementation; growth describes scaling under a cost model.

questions.question: For an array problem, what is a typical input-size measure n?
questions.correctAnswer: The number of elements.
questions.explanation: Array length describes problem size independently of the execution machine.

questions.question: What does time complexity describe?
options: How the number of basic operations grows with input size.
Only the amount of stored input.
questions.correctAnswer: How the number of basic operations grows with input size.
questions.explanation: It describes computational work as a function of size, not memory or correctness.

questions.question: Which resource must be included when analyzing a recursive algorithm's auxiliary space?
options: Every call ever made, all added together regardless of lifetime.
The memory of simultaneously active calls.
questions.correctAnswer: The memory of simultaneously active calls.
questions.explanation: Stack space depends on active recursion depth and local storage per call, not total historical calls.

questions.question: A computation repeatedly reuses a fixed number of scalar variables. What is their storage growth?
questions.explanation: Reusing the same fixed storage does not allocate a new variable for each operation.

questions.question: An n by n matrix has which storage growth when each entry occupies constant space?
questions.correctAnswer: Θ(n²)
questions.explanation: There are n² stored entries.

questions.question: An input array takes Θ(n) space and the algorithm adds only two scalar variables. Which statement is correct?
options: Total and auxiliary storage must both be Θ(1).
Total storage can be Θ(n) while auxiliary storage is Θ(1).
questions.correctAnswer: Total storage can be Θ(n) while auxiliary storage is Θ(1).
questions.explanation: Total storage may include the input; auxiliary storage counts additional working memory.

questions.question: For a fixed input size, what is the worst-case running time?
options: The cost averaged over a chosen distribution.
The maximum cost over all inputs of that size.
The cost of whichever input was tested first.
questions.correctAnswer: The maximum cost over all inputs of that size.
questions.explanation: Worst case takes a maximum; average and best case are different functions.

questions.question: What additional assumption is needed to define average-case running time?
options: That all machines have equal speed.
That every input is the worst case.
questions.correctAnswer: A probability distribution over inputs.
questions.explanation: An expectation needs a distribution specifying how inputs are weighted.

questions.question: In a left-to-right linear scan, where is a present target in the best case?
questions.correctAnswer: At the first position inspected.
questions.explanation: A first-position match ends the scan after constant work.

questions.question: Which order is increasing for sufficiently large n?
options: log n, n², n, n log n
log n, n, n log n, n²
n, log n, n², n log n
n², n log n, n, log n
questions.correctAnswer: log n, n, n log n, n²
questions.explanation: Logarithmic growth is below linear, then linearithmic, then quadratic.

questions.question: What is the tight asymptotic class of 7n³ + 25n + 60?
questions.correctAnswer: Θ(n³)
questions.explanation: The positive cubic term dominates lower-order terms.

questions.question: What is the tight asymptotic class of 50n log n + 20n?
questions.correctAnswer: Θ(n log n)
questions.explanation: The n log n term dominates n for large n.

questions.question: What is the tight asymptotic class of the positive constant function f(n)=15?
questions.explanation: The function does not grow with n.

questions.question: If f(n)=3n²+17n log₂ n+1000, which upper-bound statement is correct?
options: Both f ∈ O(n²) and f ∈ O(n³).
questions.correctAnswer: Both f ∈ O(n²) and f ∈ O(n³).
questions.explanation: The function has tight quadratic growth, and cubic is also a valid looser upper bound.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] Which condition proves f ∈ O(g) for eventually nonnegative functions?
options: f(n)≥c g(n) for every sufficiently large n.
For every n there is a different c=n making the inequality true.
There are c>0 and n₀ such that f(n)≤c g(n) for every n≥n₀.
The inequality holds for one large input size.
questions.correctAnswer: There are c>0 and n₀ such that f(n)≤c g(n) for every n≥n₀.
questions.explanation: Big-O requires a fixed positive multiplier and an eventual upper bound across all larger inputs.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] Which inequality direction is needed for an Ω(g) lower bound?
questions.correctAnswer: f(n)≥c g(n) eventually, with c>0.
questions.explanation: Omega requires f to be at least a positive constant multiple of g eventually.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] What is sufficient to establish f ∈ Θ(g)?
options: Prove both f ∈ O(g) and f ∈ Ω(g).
Show the average of f and g is small.
questions.correctAnswer: Prove both f ∈ O(g) and f ∈ Ω(g).
questions.explanation: Theta requires matching upper and lower asymptotic bounds.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] In an asymptotic proof, may c depend on n?
options: Only for Big-O, never for Omega.
No; c must be a fixed positive constant.
Yes; choosing c=n always proves the desired class.
Only when the function is a polynomial.
questions.correctAnswer: No; c must be a fixed positive constant.
questions.explanation: The existence of constants independent of input size is essential to the definitions.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] Why is checking an inequality only at n=100 insufficient?
options: The definition requires it only at n=1.
The definition requires it for every n beyond some threshold.
questions.correctAnswer: The definition requires it for every n beyond some threshold.
questions.explanation: A single successful example does not establish an eventual bound.

questions.question: What does Θ(n²) mean by itself?
options: The cost is necessarily an average-case cost.
The cost equals exactly n² operations for every n.
The cost is necessarily a best-case cost.
A tight quadratic bound on the cost function being discussed.
questions.correctAnswer: A tight quadratic bound on the cost function being discussed.
questions.explanation: Theta gives a tight growth class; best, worst and average specify which cost function is bounded.

questions.question: Why are log₂ n and log₁₀ n in the same Θ class?
options: The logarithm bases become equal as n grows.
All increasing functions have the same Θ class.
Changing a fixed logarithm base multiplies by a positive constant.
questions.correctAnswer: Changing a fixed logarithm base multiplies by a positive constant.
questions.explanation: The change-of-base formula gives a constant ratio.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] What must accompany an induction hypothesis in a correctness proof?
options: A valid base case and a justified induction step.
A claim that all smaller cases are false.
questions.correctAnswer: A valid base case and a justified induction step.
questions.explanation: Induction establishes a starting case and shows the property follows for the next case from the hypothesis.

questions.question: If a cost is exactly proportional to n², approximately what happens when n doubles?
options: It increases by a factor of 4.
It increases by a factor of 8.
It increases by a factor of 2.
questions.correctAnswer: It increases by a factor of 4.
questions.explanation: Substituting 2n gives (2n)²=4n².
